title: List workouts
description:
Write three list functions. None of them may change the list they are given.

```python
def second_largest(xs): ...     # the second largest DISTINCT value, or None if there is none
def without(xs, value): ...     # a new list with the first occurrence of value removed (an unchanged copy if it is not there)
def rotate(xs, k): ...          # a new list rotated k places to the right: rotate([1, 2, 3, 4], 1) == [4, 1, 2, 3]
```

`rotate` works for any `k`, including negative values (to the left) and values larger than the length; rotating an empty list gives an empty list.
hints: Each `def` is a small function: it receives values in its brackets and hands a result back with `return`. A `return` inside an `if` ends the function there. Lesson 3.01 covers functions in full.
`sorted(xs)` gives a sorted copy, so every copy of the largest value ends up at the end. `count` tells you how many copies there are, and the value just before them is the answer.
`remove` changes the list it is called on and fails if the value is missing, so work on `xs.copy()` and check with `in` first.
`k % len(xs)` brings any rotation into the range 0 to `len(xs) - 1`, negative ones included; then the answer is the last `k` items followed by the rest.
unitTests:
@test("second largest")
def _():
    check_eq(second_largest([3, 9, 4, 9]), 4)
    check_eq(second_largest([5, 5, 5]), None)
    check_eq(second_largest([]), None)
    check_eq(second_largest([-1, -7]), -7)
    xs = [2, 8, 5]
    second_largest(xs)
    check_eq(xs, [2, 8, 5])

@test("without")
def _():
    xs = [1, 2, 1, 3, 1]
    check_eq(without(xs, 1), [2, 1, 3, 1])
    check_eq(xs, [1, 2, 1, 3, 1])
    check_eq(without(xs, 3), [1, 2, 1, 1])
    check_eq(without(xs, 7), [1, 2, 1, 3, 1])
    check(without(xs, 7) is not xs, "without must return a new list")
    check_eq(without([], 1), [])

@test("rotate")
def _():
    xs = [1, 2, 3, 4]
    check_eq(rotate(xs, 1), [4, 1, 2, 3])
    check_eq(rotate(xs, -1), [2, 3, 4, 1])
    check_eq(rotate(xs, 6), [3, 4, 1, 2])
    check_eq(rotate(xs, 0), [1, 2, 3, 4])
    check(rotate(xs, 0) is not xs, "rotate must return a new list")
    check_eq(xs, [1, 2, 3, 4])
    check_eq(rotate([], 3), [])
